runcode: Executes arbitrary code on the live server.
Disable it in server.cfg unless actively developing, and restrict its ACE to trusted identifiers only.

sv_scriptHookAllowed.msg: ScriptHook allowed: clients can load external mod menus.
sv_scriptHookAllowed.advice: Set sv_scriptHookAllowed false unless you have a specific reason.

sv_pureLevel.msg: Pure level 0: clients may modify their game files.
sv_pureLevel.advice: Raise to sv_pureLevel 1 (or 2) to make client-side cheating harder.

sv_enforceGameBuild.advice: Pin sv_enforceGameBuild so clients run a known build.

sv_enforceSteamAuth.advice: Optional: enabling it adds a Steam identifier per player.

common_ports.name: txAdmin web panel
common_ports.advice: Port OPEN. The txAdmin panel is reachable from the internet. Risk depends on password strength + 2FA; restrict by firewall/VPN to remove exposure entirely.

common_ports.name: txAdmin alt panel
common_ports.advice: Port OPEN. Alternate txAdmin panel reachable. Same as 40120: restrict by firewall/VPN.

common_ports.name: FiveM game/API port
common_ports.advice: Port OPEN. This is the FiveM game port and is expected to be open. To hide the real IP from scrapers, use sv_forceIndirectListing true + a proxy.

common_ports.name: MySQL / MariaDB
common_ports.advice: Port OPEN. The database is reachable from the internet - this is dangerous regardless of password. Bind MySQL to 127.0.0.1 and firewall the port now.

common_ports.name: SSH
common_ports.advice: Port OPEN. SSH is reachable. Not a flaw by itself; risk depends on config. Use key-only auth, disable root login, add fail2ban/lockout.

common_ports.name: RDP (Windows remote desktop)
common_ports.advice: Port OPEN. RDP is reachable. This is NOT a breach by itself - logging in still needs valid Windows credentials you control. The real risk is automated password-guessing against an exposed port: safe with a strong unique password + account lockout, dangerous with a weak/reused one. Best practice is to not expose it at all (VPN or IP allowlist).

code_patterns.msg: Runs OS shell commands from a game script.
code_patterns.advice: No normal resource shells out. Treat as compromised unless you added it deliberately.

code_patterns.msg: Writes to server config or another resource (reinjection).
code_patterns.advice: This is how backdoors survive deletion. Remove it and audit other resources for injected lines.
Trace what goes into load(). If fetched or decoded, treat as malicious.

code_patterns.msg: Runs code from a variable at runtime.
code_patterns.advice: Hardcoded literals are lower risk; downloaded/decoded input is a red flag.
Confirm every add_ace/add_principal is yours. Unknown identifiers = backdoor.
Check why this resource reads the secret and where it sends it.
Decode and confirm the content is harmless.
Decode and inspect; long random blobs in game code deserve scrutiny.
Confirm the webhook is yours and sends no player data.
